us.summary: The company that sells Meta its AI chips is now buying a piece of Meta itself. NVIDIA is putting $3 billion into Meta's stock offering, making Jensen Huang's chip giant a shareholder in one of its biggest customers. In this video, Eric Bleeker, CFA, Chief Investment Officer of 24/7 Wall St., examines why Meta Platforms (NASDAQ: META) is raising as much as $95 billion, and what NVIDIA (NASDAQ: NVDA) gets beyond the shares. With Meta guiding to as much as $145 billion in capital spending and posting negative free cash flow, the biggest questions are whether this is smart partnership or circular financing, and how much dilution Meta shareholders should expect. We'll also look at Muse, Meta's personal AI agent, which signed up more than 10 million users in about six weeks and could drive years of demand for NVIDIA hardware. Finally, we'll discuss the two numbers that will decide whether this spending pays off: Meta's AI revenue starting in 2027, and Zuckerberg's goal of making Muse more than 10 times cheaper to run.
